subtype: Approach: consulting a teacher or counsellor about pace [Action]
passage:
Chetan: Good evening Sir, can I ask something about pace? 🙏
Vijay Sir: Yes, go ahead.
Chetan: The batch is on chapter 9 of mechanics and I'm still on chapter 5. Is it realistic to catch up before December?
Vijay Sir: Which chapters are unfinished?
Chetan: 6, 7 and 8 mainly.
Vijay Sir: For your paper, 7 carries less weight. Do 6 and 8 fully, read 7 lightly. Core first, extras later.
Chetan: Should I still attend every class?
Vijay Sir: Come to the ones on core topics. Send me your test scores next week and we'll adjust.
(next day)
Chetan: The school counsellor Ma'am said much the same and gave me a weekly plan.
Chetan: Thank you, Sir 👍

qa.q: Which chapters did Vijay Sir say to do fully?
What might Chetan be worried about at the start?
qa.a: Falling behind the batch and not being able to catch up before December.

qa.q: What else could Chetan do to keep the plan on track, and why?
qa.a: Keep a small weekly chart of progress and send scores as Sir suggested, so the plan can be adjusted with evidence.

qa.q: How does Chetan's question look to Vijay Sir?
qa.a: Vijay Sir sees a student asking early and honestly instead of struggling silently, so he can guide the focus and follow up on the scores.

grounding: A student asks a coaching mentor and a school counsellor about pace and gets advice to focus on core topics.
